rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells the person who made others despair of His mercy in worldly life that He will make him despair of His mercy today.
rows.anchor: إنك كنت تقنط الناس من رحمتي في الدنيا، فأنا اليوم أقنطك من رحمتي.

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد
rows.claim: Asma bint Yazid reports that the Prophet recited the verse and added that God forgives all sins without concern; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: عن أسماء بنت يزيد قالت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: A reading in the codex of Abdullah adds that God forgives all sins for whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله: (إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء)

rows.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Jawza says he knew no scholar or Companion of Muhammad who declared that God would not forgive a particular sin; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء قال: ما علمت أحدا من أهل العلم

rows.speaker: ثوبان
rows.claim: Thawban reports that the Prophet prized this verse above the world; when asked whether it included one who associated partners, he answered yes three times.
rows.anchor: أنه سمع ثوبان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: سمعت رسول الله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin reports Ali's judgment that no Qur'anic verse is more expansive in hope than this verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن سيرين قال: قال علي رضي الله عنه: ما في القرآن آية أوسع

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Sha'tir ibn Shakl reports Ibn Masud calling this the Qur'an's most hope-giving verse.
rows.anchor: عن شتير بن شكل قال: سمعت ابن مسعود يقول: إن أكثر آية فرجا

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri tells how Umar brought a weeping youth to the Prophet; the youth confessed grave robbery and intercourse with a corpse, and the Prophet taught that God forgives immense sins absent shirk or murder. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن معمر عن الزهري قال: دخل عمر بن الخطاب على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation says Gabriel relayed God's questions about who created, provides for, and accepts repentance from creatures; God ordered the youth forgiven, and the Prophet accepted his repentance.
rows.anchor: فدعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الشاب فتاب عليه وقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anibū means accept and return to God through obedience; submit and humble yourselves before punishment arrives, when no help will come.
rows.anchor: وأنيبوا إلى ربكم أي واقبلوا وارجعوا إليه بالطاعة.

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet saying that a servant's good fortune includes a long life and God's granting him repentance and return to Him; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Thaʿlabi adopts al-Hasan's gloss: follow God's obedience and avoid disobedience; revelation mentions evil to shun, lesser things not to desire, and good to prefer.
rows.anchor: ما قال الحسن: التزموا طاعته واجتنبوا معصيته، فإن الذي أنزل على ثلاثة أوجه:

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the best revealed thing as what God commanded in the Book.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قال السدي: الأحسن ما أمر الله به في الكتاب.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the best revealed things are the decisive verses; knowledge of the ambiguous verses is left to their Knower.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد (واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم) يعني المحكمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction means lest a soul say, as in the constructions an tamīda bikum and an taṣūmū.
rows.anchor: أن تقول نفس يعني لأن لا تقول كقوله: أن تميد بكم وأن تصوموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā ḥasratā means my regret and sorrow: grief over what is lost and cannot be recovered; Arabs replace the first-person yāʾ with alif in cries, sometimes adding hāʾ.
rows.anchor: يا حسرتى يا ندامتا وحزني، والتحسر الاغتمام على ما فات

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads the cry as yā ḥasratāy, retaining the possessive yāʾ after the alif.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قرأ أبو جعفر: يا حسرتاي.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra cites the cry yā marḥabāh as evidence for the vocative alif form; Arabs may append yāʾ after the alif to mark possession.
rows.anchor: أنشد الفراء: يا مرحباه بحمار ناجية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains falling short in God's side as falling short in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: في طاعة الله.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains the phrase as falling short regarding God's right and affair.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: في حق الله في أمر الله.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as falling short in God's affair.
rows.anchor: في حق الله في أمر الله. قاله مجاهد.

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The language scholars explain the idiom as meaning in the matter of God, like calling something small beside a past affair.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: هذا كما يقال هذا صغير في جنب ذلك الماضي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes it as God's path and religion; Arabic calls a means or path to something its side, as a poet says he endured bitterness for your sake.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في سبيل الله ودينه. والعرب تسمي السبب والطريق الى الشيء جنبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean the side leading to God's pleasure and reward; Arabic also uses junb for a side, as a poet contrasts people on one side and the prince on another.
rows.anchor: وقال في الجانب الذي يؤدي إلى رضى الله تعالى وثوابه، والعرب تسمي الجانب جنبا.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited line الناس جنب والأمير جنب demonstrates junb meaning a side, with people on one side and the ruler on the other.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: الناس جنب والأمير جنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regretful speaker admits mocking God's religion, Book, Messenger, and believers.
rows.anchor: المستهزئين بدين الله تعالى وكتابه ورسوله والمؤمنين.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the person not only neglected God's obedience but went further and mocked those who obeyed Him.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: في هذه الآية لم يكفه ان ضيع طاعة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih tells of an Israelite scholar who abandoned learning for vice after Satan promised him a long life and later repentance; dying in sin, he regretted spending life obeying Satan, and God revealed his story. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي صالح: (يا حسرتى على ما فرطت في جنب الله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lost person imagines that divine guidance would have made him God-fearing, then wishes for another return to worldly life so he could be among the virtuous.
rows.anchor: أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين أو تقول حين ترى العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabi says there are two analyses for the accusative of fa-akūna, but this excerpt does not supply them.
rows.anchor: وفي نصب قوله: (فأكون) وجهان:

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpreters take udʿūnī to mean remembrance, supplication, and asking.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو الذكر والدعاء والسؤال.

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet instructing people to ask God for every need, even a sandal strap when it breaks; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators interpret God's worship here as His oneness and obedience.
rows.anchor: إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي توحيدي وطاعتي، عن أكثر المفسرين.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reads the phrase as referring to God's supplication.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: عن دعائي.

rows.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
rows.claim: Al-Nuʿman ibn Bashir reports the Prophet saying supplication is worship and then reciting this verse; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «الدعاء هو العبادة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: When asked to pray for him, Sufyan answered that abandoning sins is itself supplication.
rows.anchor: قيل لسفيان: ادع الله. قال: إن ترك الذنوب هو الدعاء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Jaʿfar, and Abu Hatim read the verb passively, with ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on khāʾ; the source notes disagreement among other readers.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وأبو حاتم: بضم الياء وفتح الخاء.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم
rows.claim: The source reports disagreement about this reading from Abu Amr and Asim and others, without clearly assigning each alternative in the excerpt.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عمرو وعاصم غير هم ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dākhirīn means humbled and abased.
rows.anchor: جهنم داخرين صاغرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the night for rest and the day illuminating; this is His favor to people, though most do not thank Him.
rows.anchor: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن الله لذو فضل على الناس

words: ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the Creator of everything; turning away from truth despite clear proofs is the same misdirection that befalls those who deny God's signs.
rows.anchor: كذلك كما أفكتم عن الحق مع قيام الدلائل، كذلك يؤفك الذين كانوا بآيات الله يجحدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the earth a stable dwelling and the sky a canopy, fashioned people beautifully, and provided them good things.
rows.anchor: الله الذي جعل لكم الأرض قرارا والسماء بناء وصوركم فأحسن صوركم.

rows.speaker: أبو رزين العقيلي
rows.claim: The common reading has ḍamma on ṣād in ṣuwarikun; Abu Razin al-ʿUqayli reads ṣiwārikum with kasra, a dialect form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رزين العقيلي: وأحسن صوركم بكسر الصاد، وهي لغة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Call God while making religion sincere for Him.
rows.anchor: فادعوه مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين

words: قُلْ إِنِّى نُهِيتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When clear proofs came, Muhammad was commanded to say he was forbidden to worship those invoked besides God and ordered to submit to the Lord of the worlds, after being called to unbelief.
rows.anchor: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله لما جاءني البينات

words: وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَهُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had God willed, He would have made people one community on one religion; instead He admits whom He wills into His mercy, while wrongdoers have no protector or helper.
rows.anchor: ولو شاء الله لجعلهم أمة واحدة على ملة واحدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the protector; there is no protector besides Him.
rows.anchor: فالله هو الولي لا سواه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression that God gives life to the dead is an idiomatic way of saying that He revives the dead.
rows.anchor: وهو يحي الموتى مجازه: لأنه يحيي الموتى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is powerful in matters of religion, and whatever people dispute in religion is judged by God.
rows.anchor: وهو على كل شيء في الدين. قدير وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء في الدين. فحكمه إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker declares God his Lord, trusts in Him, and turns back to Him.
rows.anchor: ذلكم الله ربي عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب فاطر السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made human spouses from humankind; the source explains this as Eve being created from Adam's rib, and God also made pairs among livestock.
rows.anchor: جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا حلائل-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadhraʾukum means He creates and multiplies you; fīhi can refer to the womb, the belly, the spirit, or this mode of creation.
rows.anchor: يذرؤكم يخلقكم ويعيشكم فيه أي في الرحم، وقيل: في البطن، وقيل: في الروح

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase as generation following generation.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: نسلا بعد نسل

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan takes fī as meaning by and glosses the clause as making you numerous.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كيسان: يكثركم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis treats mithl as an added particle for emphasis, so the phrase means nothing is like Him; the verse in 2:137 and poetry illustrate this usage.
rows.anchor: ليس كمثله شيء المثل صلة ومجازه: ليس كهو شيء، فأدخل المثل توكيدا للكلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats kāf as added, yielding the meaning nothing resembles Him; the source cites a rajaz line and another poem for redundant kāf.
rows.anchor: وقيل: (الكاف) صلة مجازه: ليس مثله، كقول الراجز:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed for the community the religion He enjoined on Noah, whom Thaʿlabi calls the first prophet given a revealed law, and also revealed to Muhammad and enjoined on Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
rows.anchor: شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا وهو أول أنبياء الشريعة.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the shared command is to permit what God made lawful and forbid what He made forbidden.
rows.anchor: فقال قتادة: تحليل الحلال وتحريم الحرام،

rows.speaker: الحكم
rows.claim: Al-Hakam identifies the shared command as prohibiting sisters, mothers, and daughters.
rows.anchor: وقال الحكم: تحريم الأخوات والأمهات والبنات،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says every prophet was commanded to establish prayer, give alms, and acknowledge obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لم يبعث الله تعالى نبيا إلا أوصاه بإقامة الصلاة، وإيتاء الزكاة

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي الكتاني
rows.claim: Al-Kattani calls God subtle in kindness toward servants who, after despairing of people, take refuge in Him, trust Him, and return; God then accepts them and turns toward them.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن علي الكتاني: اللطيف بمن لجأ إليه من عباده إذا أيس من الخلق،

rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الوهاب الثقفي
rows.claim: A poem recited by Thaʿlabi says God apportions each person's provision and is kind to the one who seeks refuge in Him, illustrating al-Laṭīf.
rows.anchor: أنشدني أبو علي محمد بن عبد الوهاب الثقفي:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One gloss says God makes His servants' virtues known while concealing their faults.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اللطيف الذي ينشر من عباده المناقب، ويستر عليه المثالب،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says God accepts little and gives much.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي يقبل القليل، ويبذل الجزيل،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss describes God as mending the broken and making the difficult easy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي يجبر الكسير، وييسر العسير،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says no one despairs of God's provision in this world and no believer despairs of His merciful pardon.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي لا ييأس أحد في الدنيا من رزقه، ولا ييأس مؤمن في العفو من رحمته.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says only God's justice is feared and only His bounty is hoped for.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي لا يخاف إلا عدله، ولا يرجى إلا فضله،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says God gives a servant blessings beyond aspiration and imposes obedience within capacity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي يبذل لعبده النعمة، فوق الهمة ويكلفه الطاعة دون الطاقة،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says God does not hasten punishment for the disobedient and does not disappoint one who hopes in Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي لا يعاجل من عصاه ولا يخيب من رجاه،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says God does not turn away a petitioner or make a hopeful person despair.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي لا يرد سائله ولا يؤيس آمله،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss defines al-Laṭīf as the One who pardons a person who slips.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي يعفو عمن يهفو،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says God has mercy on one who has no mercy on himself.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي يرحم من لا يرحم نفسه،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says God helps a servant perform service and then multiplies His praise of him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي يعين على الخدمة، ثم يكثر المدحة،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An inward gloss says God lights in knowers' hearts a lamp of witnessing, makes the straight path their way, and sends down abundant generosity upon them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي أوقد في أسرار عارفيه من المشاهدة سراجا، وجعل الصراط المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides as He wills: expansively or sparingly, little or much, lawful or unlawful, in ease or hardship, at home or abroad, by measure or without measure.
rows.anchor: يرزق من يشاء كما يشاء من شاء موسعا، ومن شاء مقترا، ومن شاء قليلا ومن شاء كثيرا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever seeks the afterlife through deeds has that harvest multiplied from tenfold onward as God wills; whoever works for worldly gain receives some of it and has no share in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: من كان يريد حرث الآخرة يعني يريد بعمله الآخرة. نزد له في حرثه بالتضعيف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the afterlife-seeker gains an increased harvest, while one who prefers this world gets only his allotted worldly provision and no afterlife share except the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: يقول: من عمل لآخرته نزد له في حرثه

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar classifies deeds in four ways: righteous work aimed at worldly gain earns no afterlife share; ostentation earns only woe; righteous work for God and the afterlife earns Paradise and worldly blessings; sinful work earns punishment unless God pardons. He cites 11:15.
rows.anchor: إن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه، قال: الأعمال على أربعة وجوه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage asks whether the idolaters have partners who legislated a religion without God's permission; absent the decree of judgment at the appointed Resurrection, they would already have been judged.
rows.anchor: أم لهم شركاء شرعوا لهم من الدين ما لم يأذن به الله ولولا كلمة الفصل يوم القيامة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers, meaning the polytheists, will be fearful because of their deeds, and the punishment will certainly befall them.
rows.anchor: ترى الظالمين المشركين يوم القيامة مشفقين وجلين. مما كسبوا وهو واقع بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who did good will be in the gardens of Paradise, receiving whatever they wish from their Lord; this is the great bounty.
rows.anchor: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في روضات الجنات لهم ما يشاؤن عند ربهم ذلك هو الفضل الكبير.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God did not withdraw the Qur'an despite the first community's rejection; in mercy He repeatedly presented it and called them to it for twenty years or as long as He willed.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: والله لو كان هذا القرآن رفع حين رده أوائل هذه الأمة لهلكوا،

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the rebuke as asking whether God should leave people neglected, neither commanding nor forbidding them.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: أفنترككم سدى لا نأمركم ولا ننهاكم.

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi glosses it as asking whether God should fold the reminder away so people are neither called nor admonished.
rows.anchor: الكسائي: أفنطوي عنكم الذكر طيا، فلا تدعون ولا توعظون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ḍaraba ʿanhu ṣafḥan is eloquent Qur'anic Arabic for turning away; its image is presenting the side of one's neck, and Arab usage also means to leave something aside. Kathir's poem illustrates ṣafūḥā as turning away.
rows.anchor: وهذا من فصيحات القرآن، والعرب تقول لمن أمسك عن الشيء وأعرض عنه: ضرب عنه صفحا،

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والكوفة إلا عاصما
rows.claim: The Medinan and Kufan readers except Asim read an with an alif and take it as idh, as in the cited Qur'anic examples.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والكوفة إلا عاصما أن تكتب الألف على معنى إذ.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Other readers use fatḥ on an with the sense because; Abu Ubayda prefers the accusative because God rebukes them for past conduct He already knew.
rows.anchor: النصب أحب إلي لأن الله تعالى عاتبهم على ما كان منهم وعلمه قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description qawman musrifīn means polytheists who transgress God's command.
rows.anchor: قوما مسرفين مشركين متجاوزين أمر الله.

words: مِن نَّبِىٍّ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples mocked every prophet, as Muhammad's people mock him; this consoles the Prophet. God destroyed communities stronger than them, leaving the pattern and punishment of former peoples as an example.
rows.anchor: من نبي إلا كانوا به يستهزؤن كاستهزاء قومك بك.

words: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If asked who created the heavens and earth, the polytheists acknowledge the mighty, knowing Creator.
rows.anchor: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the earth a cradle and set paths through it so people could find their way.
rows.anchor: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وجعل لكم فيها سبلا لعلكم تهتدون

words: وَٱلَّذِى نَزَّلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۢ بِقَدَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends rain in the amount people need; with it He revives dead land, just as people will be raised alive from their graves.
rows.anchor: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر أي بمقدار حاجتكم إليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as rain revives dead land, the dead will come out alive from their graves.
rows.anchor: تخرجون من قبوركم أحياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-azwāj means the various kinds or classes.
rows.anchor: والذي خلق الأزواج الأصناف.

words: وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْفُلْكِ وَٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ مَا تَرْكَبُونَ
rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The plural ẓuhūr is attached to the singular mā because that singular has a collective sense, like army, host, and cavalry.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: أضاف الظهور إلى الواحد لأنه ذلك الواحد في معنى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ẓuhūrihi is singular because it refers back to the collective mā, which can denote the riding animals together.
rows.anchor: لتستووا على ظهوره ذكر الكناية لأنه ردها إلى ما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqrinīn means able to master or control it; the sense is that people could not match its strength.
rows.anchor: أي مطبقين ضابطين قاهرين وهو من القرآن، كأنه أراد وما كنا مقاومين له في القوة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munqalibūn means that people will return to God at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون لمنصرفون في المعاد.

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said bismillah when placing his foot in the stirrup, then on mounting praised God, recited these verses, and repeated takbīr and tahlīl three times each. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، إنه كان إذا وضع رجله في الركاب،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the verse teaches what to say when riding ships or livestock and cites the prayer for a blessed landing from 23:29.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: في هذه الآية يعلمكم كيف تقولون إذا ركبتم في الفلك والأنعام تقولون:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists assigned God a share or portion from among His servants.
rows.anchor: وجعلوا يعني هؤلاء المشركين له من عباده جزءا أي نصيبا وبعضا.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil and Qatada take juzʾ as a counterpart, referring to their claim that angels are God's daughters.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل وقتادة: عدلا وذلك قولهم للملائكة هم بنات الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being is plainly ungrateful.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان لكفور مبين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks whether the polytheists witnessed the angels' creation and thus knew they were female.
rows.anchor: أشهدوا أحضروا خلقهم حتى يعرفوا إنهم إناث،

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The Medinan reading uses the passive, meaning that they were brought to witness the angels' creation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة أشهدوا على غير تسمية الفاعل أي أحضروا.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi take the objects of their worship to be the angels.
rows.anchor: وقالوا لو شاء الرحمن ما عبدناهم يعني الملائكة في قول قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid instead takes the objects of worship to be idols; the polytheists claimed God's failure to punish them showed His approval, but God says they have no knowledge and only conjecture.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني الأوثان، وإنما لم يعجل عقوبتنا على عبادتنا إياها لرضا منا بعبادتها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether God gave them a scripture before the Qur'an to which they could cling.
rows.anchor: أم آتيناهم كتابا من قبله أي من قبل هذا القرآن. فهم به مستمسكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they found their forefathers following a religion and are guided by their ancestors' footsteps.
rows.anchor: بل قالوا إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة دين. وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: The common reading has ḍamma on the initial hamza and means religion or creed; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and Mujahid read the word with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة (أمة) بضم الألف، وهي الدين والملة، وقرأ عمر بن عبد العزيز ومجاهد أمة بكسر الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the kasra reading, one explanation is a way or purpose, from the verb meaning to intend; another is blessing, as Adi ibn Zayd's verse uses umma; alternatively both are dialect forms with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هي الطريقة والمقصد من قولهم أممت، وقيل: هي النعمة. قال عدي بن زيد:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In every town, its affluent people answered a warner as Muhammad's people did, appealing to ancestral religion; muqtadūn means following and emulating them.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ما أرسلنا من قبلك في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: The common reading makes the word an imperative, while Ibn Amir reads it as a statement; a similar reading is reported from Hafs ibn Asim.
rows.anchor: قال قراءة العامة على الأمر، وقرأ ابن عامر على الخبر ومثله روى حفص بن عاصم.

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads jāʾakum, while the other readers read jiʾtukum in the singular.
rows.anchor: أولو جاءكم بالألف أبو جعفر. الباقون جئتكم على الواحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahdā means a sounder or more correct religion than the one inherited from their fathers.
rows.anchor: بأهدى بدين أصوب. مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God took vengeance on those who rejected the messengers and tells the audience to observe the end of the deniers.
rows.anchor: قالوا إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون فانتقمنا منهم. فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barāʾ means innocent or free of; it is an indeclinable verbal noun used as an adjective, while Abdullah's reading has the adjective barīʾ.
rows.anchor: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه وقومه إنني براء أي بريء، ولا يثنى البراء ولا يجمع ولا يؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham disavows every object of worship except his Creator, who will guide him to His religion.
rows.anchor: إلا الذي فطرني خلقني، ومجاز الآية: إنني براء من كل معبود إلا الذي فطرني

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada identify the enduring word in Abraham's descendants as lā ilāha illā Allāh.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: يعني لا إله إلا الله،

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi identifies it as Abraham's testament to his children that remained in his descendants, the testament mentioned in 2:132.
rows.anchor: وقال القرظي: يعني وجعل وصية إبراهيم التي أوصى بها بنيه باقية في نسله وذريته

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the enduring saying as I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds and cites the statement that God named the community Muslims in 22:78.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: يعني قوله

rows.speaker: أبو قرصافة
rows.claim: Abu Qursafa reports the Prophet saying that removing rubbish from a mosque is a dowry for the houris; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن عزة بنت أبي قرصافة، عن أبيها قال: سمعت رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruits of Paradise are always available and free of harmful effects; Qatada adds that its inhabitants are safe from death, ailments, and Satan.
rows.anchor: آمنين من نفادها وعدمها في بعض الأزمنة ومن غائلتها ومضرتها،

words: لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ إِلَّا ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means after the first death: illa stands in place of baʿda, as in 4:22, and like saying one has eaten no food today except what one ate yesterday.
rows.anchor: يعني سوى الموتة الأولى وبعدها وضع (إلا) موضع بعد كقوله: ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's protection of the people of Paradise from Hell's punishment is a favor from Him and the great triumph.
rows.anchor: ووقاهم عذاب الجحيم فضلا من ربك ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the statement that God made it easy by Muhammad's tongue, the pronoun refers to an unstated Qur'an.
rows.anchor: فإنما يسرناه سهلناه، كناية عن غير مذكور.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to await victory and help from God, while the opponents await, in their claim, his defeat.
rows.anchor: فارتقب فانتظر الفتح والنصر من ربك. إنهم مرتقبون بزعمهم قهرك.
